## Solution

Let $v: K^\times \to \Gamma$ be the valuation, with $A = \{x \in K : v(x) \geq 0\}$ and maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m} = \{x \in A : v(x) > 0\}$.

### Prime ideals ↔ convex subgroups

There is a well-known order-reversing bijection between prime ideals of $A$ and convex subgroups of $\Gamma$. Given a prime $p$, the associated convex subgroup is
$$\Delta := v\bigl((A\setminus p)\bigr) = \{v(s) : s \in A,\; s\notin p\}\;\subseteq\;\Gamma.$$
Equivalently, $A\setminus p = \{s\in A : v(s)\in\Delta\}$, and
$$p = \{x\in A : v(x)\notin \Delta\} = \{x\in A : v(x)>\delta\ \text{for all}\ \delta\in\Delta\}.$$
(For $x\in A$ we have $v(x)\geq 0 = 0\in\Delta$; if $v(x)\notin\Delta$ then by convexity $v(x)$ must exceed every element of $\Delta$.)

### Value group of $A_p$

$A_p$ is a valuation ring of $K$ (localization of a valuation ring at a prime is a valuation ring). Its units satisfy:
$$x\in A_p^\times \iff x\in A_p\ \text{and}\ x^{-1}\in A_p \iff v(x)\in\Delta.$$

*Proof.* If $x\in A_p^\times$, write $x=a/s$ with $a\in A$, $s\in A\setminus p$. Then $x^{-1}=s/a\in A_p$ forces $a\notin p$ (else $\bar a=0$), so $v(a)\in\Delta$ and $v(s)\in\Delta$, giving $v(x)=v(a)-v(s)\in\Delta$. Conversely, if $v(x)\in\Delta$: if $v(x)\geq 0$ then $x\in A\subseteq A_p$ and $v(x^{-1})=-v(x)\in\Delta\cap\Gamma_{\leq 0}$, so $x^{-1}\in A_p$ (write $x^{-1}=1/x$ with $1\in A$, $x\in A\setminus p$). If $v(x)<0$ then $x^{-1}\in A$ and $v(x^{-1})=-v(x)\in\Delta\cap\Gamma_{\geq 0}$, so $x^{-1}\in A\setminus p$ and $x=1/(x^{-1})\in A_p$. Either way $x, x^{-1}\in A_p$. ∎

The value group of the valuation ring $A_p$ is the quotient of $v(K^\times)=\Gamma$ by the unit group $v(A_p^\times)=\Delta$:
$$\boxed{\Gamma(A_p) = \Gamma/\Delta.}$$

### Value group of $A/p$

$A/p$ is a valuation ring of its fraction field $K'=\operatorname{Frac}(A/p)$: for any $\bar x\in (K')^\times$, write $\bar x=\bar a/\bar b$ with $a,b\in A$, $b\notin p$; since $A$ is a valuation ring, either $a/b\in A$ or $b/a\in A$, and $\bar a\neq 0$ forces $a\notin p$, so $\bar x\in A/p$ or $\bar x^{-1}\in A/p$.

Define $v': (K')^\times\to\Delta$ by $v'(\bar a/\bar b)=v(a)-v(b)$ for $a,b\in A\setminus p$ (so $v(a),v(b)\in\Delta$). This is well-defined: if $\bar a/\bar b=\bar c/\bar d$, then $ad=bc$ in $A$, so $v(a)+v(d)=v(b)+v(c)$, giving $v(a)-v(b)=v(c)-v(d)\in\Delta$.

The valuation ring of $v'$ is $\{\bar x\in K' : v'(\bar x)\geq 0\} = A/p$, and its unit group has value $0$, so the value group of $A/p$ is the image $v'((K')^\times)=\Delta$:
$$\boxed{\Gamma(A/p) = \Delta.}$$

### Summary

If $\Delta\subseteq\Gamma$ is the convex subgroup corresponding to $p$ (i.e. $\Delta=v(A\setminus p)$, equivalently $p=\{x\in A:v(x)\notin\Delta\}$), then:

- **$A_p$ has value group $\Gamma/\Delta$** (the coarsening of the valuation by $\Delta$),
- **$A/p$ has value group $\Delta$** (the specialization, retaining only the $\Delta$-part).

These fit the exact sequence $0\to\Delta\to\Gamma\to\Gamma/\Delta\to 0$: localization kills $\Delta$ (quotient $\Gamma/\Delta$), while the residue ring $A/p$ keeps only $\Delta$.
